Subject: Dedicated sizing for upcoming commit

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. Were evaluating a ~24 month committed plan and need a concrete sizing recommendation for dedicated capacity. A few facts from our side:
- Typical responses average ~220 tokens (generation) per request; some flows spike to ~1,200 tokens for long-form outputs.
- Expected 90-day ramp to peak: average 18M tokens/day -> peak day 60M tokens; steady peak TPS estimate ~420 tokens/sec during our regional business hours.
- Hard SLO: p95 latency for generation (up to 512 input + 220 generation) must be <= 400ms.
- We want 30-40% headroom for launches and unknown seasonal spikes.

Could you send an initial mapping (tokens/sec -> GPU count by GPU type), and any latency tradeoffs for quantization / batching? Also confirm whether Redwoods canary/fallback to hosted models will be available in the event of short-term capacity pressure.

Elena Park
Head of Platform
CometAI

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for upcoming commit — technical model attached

Hi all,

I built a quick token-flow model and a couple of GPU-mapping scenarios. Summary below and the full workbook is attached (cometai_tps_model.xlsx). Ill call out assumptions up front:
Assumptions
- Typical response token generation: 220 tokens; long-form: 1,200 tokens (10% of requests).
- Peak day profile: 420 tokens/sec sustained for a 3-hour window (conservative), ramp/decay outside window.
- Base model: fp16 A100 80GB baseline, H100 for latency-critical path if we need lower p95 for same slab. Quantization (int8) option reduces GPU cost but can add ~10-25% latency depending on kernel and model.

Scenario A (latency-first, p95 <= 400ms target)- Model: H100-80GB nodes (XLA kernels optimized).- Measured single-GPU steady-state serving: ~4,200 tokens/sec (mixed batch strategy) for your token distro using continuous batching and prefix cache warm.- To handle 420 tokens/sec sustained with 40% headroom -> target capacity = 420 * 1.4 = 588 tokens/sec. That fits comfortably on a single H100 in steady state; however, we need redundancy and canary margins.- Recommended slab: 3x H100 nodes (2 active, 1 standby) -> effective capacity ~8,400 tokens/sec active, absorbs bursts and provides failover. Expected p95 under this configuration: 180-320ms for typical requests, 350-420ms for long-form at peak if cache misses occur.

Scenario B (cost-optimized, hybrid with quantization)- Model: A100 80GB nodes with int8 quantized weights for non-critical paths.- Single-GPU steady-state: ~2,300 tokens/sec (quantized) or ~3,500 tokens/sec no-quantization depending on batching.- To meet 420 tokens/sec with 40% headroom -> 588 tokens/sec target. Quantized A100s: recommend 1x-2x nodes depending on expected long-form percentage. For redundancy, recommend 4x A100s (2 active scaled sets), effective active capacity ~6,000 tokens/sec.- Expected p95: 260-480ms (quantized long-form may hit upper bound).

Bursting and runway notes- Short-term bursts (2-5x normal TPS lasting <15 minutes) can be absorbed by automatic burst pool from Dedicated spare capacity + fallback to hosted-compatible smaller models. We recommend a committed burst allotment for the first 6 months (policy included in proposal).

Headroom and SLA fit- We recommend targeting 35-40% headroom for launches. With the H100 3-node slab were >10x your stated peak; this is intentionally conservative to ensure headroom for unexpected spikes and synthetic workloads.

Next steps
1) Confirm whether CometAI is comfortable with an H100-first slab or prefers cost-optimized A100 mapping.
2) If H100: Ill finalize the slab sizing into the proposal PDF and include a monthly burst credit line.
3) If A100: well run a short quantization latency audit (~72 hours) on a representative workload to validate p95 numbers.

Attachment: cometai_tps_model.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for upcoming commit — proposal and next steps

Elena — appreciate the patience while we modeled options. Attaching the proposal (cometai_proposal_v1.pdf) which captures two commercial options:

Option 1 (Latency-first, recommended for product launches)- 3x H100 dedicated slab (2 active + 1 standby)- Guaranteed capacity: ~8,400 tokens/sec active (ample headroom relative to 420 tps peak)- Target p95: 180-320ms typical; up to ~420ms for long-form worst-case- Monthly burst credit: 8 hours of 2x capacity with automatic scaling- Price: $XXX,XXX / month (see Proposal)

Option 2 (Cost-first, validated quantization)- 4x A100 slab with quantization fallback for non-critical flows- Approx active capacity: ~6,000 tokens/sec- Target p95: 260-480ms (quantized long-form near upper bound)- Includes 24/7 engineering guardrail and a 72-hour quantization validation window- Price: $YYY,YYY / month (see Proposal)

Other notes- Canary & fallback: Redwood will configure traffic routing so non-critical routes fail over to hosted variants during sustained capacity exhaustion; critical routes will always prefer dedicated slab and trigger alerts before fallback.- SLA: were proposing a 99.9% availability SLA for the dedicated slab with p95 latency targets tied to the chosen option.

Ben has approved a short-term onboarding discount for the first two months — details in the PDF (Ben, thanks for coordinating).

Next actions
- Elena / procurement: please review the attached proposal and the DocuSign link. If you confirm H100 well schedule a 1-hour kickoff to configure fleet, canary routes, and define the exact burst policy.
- Internal: Mina and I will prepare the deployment runbook and the scheduled quantization audit if they pick Option 2.

Thanks — looking forward to getting CometAI live.

Best,
